title: Decoder floors, case (b): excess 3 is paid (≥ 64 with ≤ 4 non-full corrections; E8 lifts ≥ 68; no κ claim)
head: 18f7d4da808edb82d32e2081f869b8c993eca891
body:
Follow-up to #2816 and #2826 (both ours). Only `research/one-sided-excess-three/` is added; nothing existing is changed. No κ claim, no supplier word, no SAT solver.

## Result

Setting as in #2816: P112, case (b), characteristic 0, every number of terms. `Δ` is the ε-free excess over 64, `n_nf` the number of non-full corrections of the normalised decoder.

* **All eight slack-3 multisets are dead.** `[7^5,6^5,2]`, `[7^5,6^5,1,1]`, `[7^4,6^6,3]`, `[7^4,6^6,1^3]`, `[7^9,4]`, `[7^9,3,1]` (`d = 8`) and `[7^3,6^6,2]`, `[7^3,6^6,1,1]` (`d = 7`) do not occur as the minimum-weight basis of `S_{≤7}`. With #2816 and #2826, no `d ≥ 1` multiset of slack ≤ 3 occurs. The kills are exact finite computations run in **two independent implementations** that agree on every rank histogram (two 6-flats plus ≤ 2 lines: span ≤ 4; two 6-flats plus a 3-flat: span ≤ 7 < 8, with exact span ≤ 4 on the 6 relaxed-rank-8 pairs (all 161,420 third flats); a 7-flat and a 4-flat: span ≤ 4; controls: two 7-flats reach rank 8 on 152 pairs, two 6-flats give span 3).
* **Carrier Lemma for `κ ≤ 3`** (written proof; the finite inputs are re-run): at most `Δ` z-carrying members of a spanning family of total weight `64 + Δ`, `Δ ≤ 7`, when the weight-≤ 7 part has cost ≤ 3. New ingredient: a Parity statement for three pairwise non-orthogonal lines (`Q` on `E8/2E8`).
* **`Δ ≤ 3 ⇒ n_nf ≤ Δ`** (decoder level) and `Δ ≤ 3 ⇒ ρ_0 ≤ Δ` (lift level).

Consequences:

* one-sided P112 decoders with **≤ 4 non-full corrections cost ≥ 64** (any number of full ones); in general `≥ 64 − max(0, n_nf − 4) ≥ 60` (was `≥ 59` in #2826);
* lift level: `cost_w(S) ≥ 64 + min(|I|, 4)`; every lift of the E8 root code has `cost_w ≥ 68` (`≥ 72` unless the P112 restriction has `Δ ≥ 4`); gain-law form `|P120| − C(P120) ≤ 52`.

The bound `≥ 64` at `n_nf = 4` is tight: the root-swap family of #2816 §6 attains exactly 64 for `n_nf = 1..4`.

## Proof and checks

Every claim in the README carries its proof (Lemma B for any `d`, the kill criterion, the Carrier Lemma with its case analysis, the peeling argument) and is labelled PROVEN / CHECKED / RECORDED / INHERITED. `verify.sh` re-runs from a fresh `git archive`: manifest, byte-identical regeneration of both data files, the slack-3 landscape (`land3.py 3`, exactly the eight survivors), the finite inputs of the Carrier and Parity Lemmas (all 112 roots and 8 frame directions: coloop structure and cocircuit sizes ≥ 5; Parity searches over all pairwise non-orthogonal triples and quadruples), and both implementations on the survivors' flat configurations and the controls, chunked (at most 3 processes, `nice -n 10`, `timeout 1200` on each, no wait loops). Then `check_logs.py` prints one PASS/FAIL line per assertion.

Not re-audited by the second implementation, and covered by written proofs or citations instead: Lemma B, completeness of the direction list for `|Off| ≤ 80` (#2826 §4), the bookkeeping of the landscape (`land3.py`, one implementation; its stages are the cited rules of #2816 and #2826), and the Parity and Carrier proofs.

## Not claimed

`Δ ≥ n_nf` for `n_nf ≥ 5`; two-sided decoders; case (c) (see #2784); P104 and other punctured units; positive characteristic.
